NEW PATIENT — establishing care

27 yo woman, graphic designer, lives in Holyoke with a roommate. Leaving her prior primary care office; wants one place that can coordinate her specialists.

HPI / PMH as she tells it:
1. Epilepsy since childhood, generalized seizures. Phenytoin 300 mg at bedtime for roughly three years now, before that other meds she can't name. Last seizure was in the spring of last year. Sees an outside neurology group about once a year.
2. HIV, diagnosed 2016. She says her count was very low when it was found ("stage 3"). Followed by an ID clinic, which moved her to Biktarvy earlier this spring; she does not remember the name of the earlier combination. Says she is taking it.
3. Depression, recurrent, with two bad episodes in her early twenties. Sertraline 100 mg has kept her steady. No psychiatrist currently; no hospitalizations. Denies SI today.
4. Folate deficiency after methotrexate in 2016 — she was given methotrexate for an ectopic pregnancy, which then ruptured and she ended up with a laparoscopic salpingectomy. Has taken folic acid 1 mg daily since, plus a prenatal vitamin ("I want a baby someday").

PSH: lap salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic 2016; D&C 2017.
Meds: phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS; Biktarvy 1 tab daily; sertraline 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: SULFA ANTIBIOTICS — anaphylaxis. Latex — contact dermatitis.
FH: father epilepsy. Mother RA and type 2 DM. Sister with major depression. Maternal aunt breast cancer at 45.
SH: never smoker. Drinks occasionally at social events. No drugs. Works as a graphic designer, mostly from home.

ROS: negative except as above. Sleep ok. Appetite ok.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing, pleasant, good eye contact. HEENT unremarkable, oropharynx clear, gums normal. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars. No edema. Neuro: alert, fluent, CN grossly intact, gait normal. Skin without rash.

PHQ-9 8.

A/P:
- Epilepsy, controlled. Continue phenytoin. Will get neurology records; level at next visit.
- HIV on Biktarvy — ID manages ART. Requesting their most recent note with CD4/VL.
- MDD, recurrent, severe by history, currently stable on sertraline 100. PHQ-9 mild range. Continue; return 6 months or sooner.
- Hx drug-induced folate deficiency — continue folic acid.
- Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, hep C Ab, hep B sAg/sAb today. Pap and vaccines at a physical next month (she would rather not do the Pap today). Pneumococcal and meningococcal vaccines indicated with HIV.
- Records release signed for prior PCP, ID, neurology.

Return ~6 weeks for physical.

documents.title: Office Visit — Thirst/Urination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: thirsty all the time, peeing constantly.

HPI: Started around February. Keeps a big water bottle at her desk and refills it "five or six times" a day. Up 3–4 times a night to urinate, which is new. Urine looks like water. No dysuria, no fever. No head injury, no new meds. No seizures. Mom has type 2 diabetes so she is worried about that.

Meds unchanged: phenytoin 300 qHS, Biktarvy, sertraline 100, folic acid, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: vitals as charted. Appears well hydrated, mucous membranes moist. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Neuro nonfocal; visual fields full to confrontation.

UA in office: very dilute, no glucose.

A/P: Polyuria/polydipsia. No glycosuria on the UA and a normal glucose on her April labs is expected — this does not look like diabetes mellitus. Dilute urine and sodium at the top of normal raise concern for diabetes insipidus. Lithium/hypercalcemia not in play; calcium pending. BMP, A1c today. Referring to endocrinology for evaluation. Told her not to restrict fluids on her own — drink to thirst. Call with confusion, vomiting or if she can't keep up with her thirst.

documents.title: Labs and endocrinology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gretchen, your A1c and glucose are normal, so this is not sugar diabetes. Your sodium is at the high end of normal and the urine is very dilute, which fits with the hormone problem we talked about (diabetes insipidus). Endocrinology has you scheduled May 15. Keep drinking to thirst until then.

documents.title: RE: Labs and endocrinology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thank you. is that related to my seizures or the hiv? just want to know what to expect

documents.title: RE: Labs and endocrinology appointment

OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP — new consultation, 05/15/2019

Referred by: PCP. Question: polyuria/polydipsia.

History: 28-year-old woman with about three months of heavy urination and constant thirst. She estimates she now drinks roughly 6 liters a day and gets up several times overnight to void. No recent head injury and no surgery of any kind near the head. Background of childhood generalized epilepsy (phenytoin), HIV on ART, recurrent depression on sertraline, prior folate deficiency.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis); latex.
Meds: phenytoin, Biktarvy, sertraline, folic acid, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: normal, including visual fields and thyroid. Not volume depleted.

Labs today:
  Sodium 148 mEq/L
  Serum osmolality 300 mOsm/kg
  Urine osmolality 150 mOsm/kg

Impression: Central diabetes insipidus, currently inadequately controlled. Concentrated plasma with inappropriately dilute urine; the clinical picture favors a central cause.

Plan:
1. Start desmopressin acetate 0.1 mg by mouth twice daily.
2. Drink to thirst only — do not force fluids on desmopressin (risk of low sodium).
3. Sodium in one week through her PCP, please.
4. Follow up here in 3 months.

Thank you for this referral.
Endocrinology attending

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN PRACTICE — preconception visit, 11/17/2020

Thank you for referring this 29-year-old (prior ruptured ectopic treated with salpingectomy; a D&C the following year) who would like to start a family and is anxious about how her medicines might affect a pregnancy. No recent illness, no medication changes, and she says she has not missed any phenytoin. Generalized epilepsy has been well controlled on phenytoin for about five years, last seizure more than three years ago. Also central DI on desmopressin, HIV on ART, recurrent depression on sertraline, history of folate deficiency, and she has been on folic acid.

Meds: phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS, desmopressin 0.1 mg BID, Biktarvy, sertraline 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, prenatal vitamin with iron.
Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: unremarkable.

Data: recent CBC normal, liver panel normal, phenytoin level therapeutic (PCP labs 10/13).

Counseling:
- Phenytoin carries a known risk of birth defects and fetal hydantoin effects; uncontrolled seizures also carry real risk to her and a fetus. Any change in her antiseizure plan should be made with neurology before conception, not after.
- Continue folic acid daily, together with the prenatal vitamin.
- ART in pregnancy: review with her ID physician before conceiving; viral suppression is the priority.
- Desmopressin may be continued in pregnancy; needs can rise.
- Early prenatal care once pregnant; will need high-risk co-management.

No medication changes today. Happy to see her once she conceives.

OB/GYN attending

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — physician record, 05/11/2023 21:40

Arrived by EMS. 32-year-old woman with generalized epilepsy since childhood and central diabetes insipidus (worse during her pregnancy in 2021) who had a seizure witnessed by her roommate and fell from a second-floor window. Roommate tells us she has had seizures since she was a child and stopped taking her medicines recently.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex.

On arrival: postictal, obtunded. T 36.5 C, HR 108, BP 138/90. Respirations irregular. Pupils sluggish to light. No purposeful response to pain; decerebrate posturing. Reflexes brisk. Intubated for airway protection (rapid sequence).

Trauma survey: no long-bone deformity, pelvis stable, chest and abdomen without injury on primary and secondary survey and on imaging.

Isotonic saline 120 mL given over the first two hours; urine output over that time 1.4 L via Foley.

Labs: Na 151, serum osm 302, urine SG 1.002, urine osm 68, glucose 110. Phenytoin level undetectable.

CT head: bilateral cerebral contusions and small intraventricular hemorrhage.

Impression: breakthrough generalized seizure from antiseizure medication nonadherence, with fall from height and traumatic brain injury (bilateral contusions, small IVH); hypernatremia with dilute high-volume urine — uncontrolled central DI off desmopressin.
Plan: fosphenytoin load, desmopressin, neurosurgery and neurology consults, admit neuro ICU.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/11/2023 (neuro ICU) — discharged 05/22/2023.

Diagnoses:
1. Generalized tonic-clonic seizure due to stopping antiseizure medication
2. Traumatic brain injury — bilateral cerebral contusions, small intraventricular hemorrhage (fall from second story during seizure)
3. Hypernatremia from uncontrolled central diabetes insipidus (missed desmopressin)
4. Medication nonadherence (had stopped all home medications)
5. HIV on ART; recurrent major depression

Course: Loaded with fosphenytoin, then phenytoin resumed at home dose. Desmopressin given IV initially; urine output fell and sodium normalized gradually over about 48 hours with free water. Neurosurgery followed — nonoperative. Repeat head CT at 24 h stable. Extubated hospital day 3, then transferred to the floor. No further seizures. Mental status improved steadily; at discharge alert, oriented, conversant, ambulating independently. PT/OT cleared for home with roommate. She told the team she stopped her pills a few weeks ago because she was "tired of being a patient"; social work and the inpatient psychiatry liaison met with her — no SI; sertraline resumed.

Allergies: SULFONAMIDES (anaphylaxis); LATEX.

Discharge medications (home regimen resumed): phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS; desmopressin 0.1 mg BID; Biktarvy 1 tab daily; sertraline 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.

Instructions: no driving for 6 months after the seizure (Massachusetts rule); no heights, bathing alone or swimming alone. Follow up with PCP within 1 week, neurology 4 weeks, endocrinology, ID.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — 05/25/2026 19:50

Brought in by her roommate, who found a suicide note in the apartment this afternoon. 36-year-old woman with childhood-onset epilepsy, central DI, advanced HIV (cerebral toxoplasmosis 2024, now suppressed), seizures, and recurrent severe major depression.

She confirms she wrote the note and says she wants to die; she feels worthless and that things are hopeless. Six months of low mood, no pleasure in anything, marked weight loss, poor sleep, trouble concentrating. She has a specific plan to overdose on her roommate's prescription medicines and has already gathered the pills. She stopped her sertraline about three months ago. Denies alcohol or drug use.

Current meds: phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS, desmopressin 0.1 mg BID, Biktarvy daily, folic acid 1 mg, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: SULFONAMIDES (anaphylaxis); LATEX.

Vitals stable. Weight 53 kg.
Exam: tearful, poor eye contact, quiet monotone speech. Physical examination otherwise unremarkable.

Labs: CBC, CMP, TSH/free T4 within normal limits.

Psychiatry consulted (see below). Roommate states she will remove and dispose of the collected pills and her own medications from the apartment; her daughter is staying with the roommate.

Impression: severe recurrent major depression with suicidal ideation, plan and preparatory behavior.
Disposition: voluntary admission, inpatient psychiatry, 5/26.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Psychiatry ED Consultation (2026-05-25)

Psychiatry consult — ED, 05/25/2026 22:30

HPI as per ED. On interview she is slowed, tearful and sparse in speech. She describes, without wavering, a conviction that her illnesses — the HIV, the seizures, the brain infection — are punishment she has earned and that she deserves to suffer; this does not shift with gentle challenge. Denies hearing voices or seeing things. No manic symptoms. Stopped sertraline ~3 months ago because "it wasn't doing anything and I didn't deserve to feel better." Collected pills for an overdose; the roommate interrupted.

MSE: thin, casually dressed, poor eye contact, psychomotor slowing, low monotone voice. Mood "empty," affect depressed and tearful. Thought process linear, slow. Thought content: suicidal ideation with plan and intent; fixed mood-congruent guilt delusion as above. No hallucinations. Insight and judgment poor.

Assessment: major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe, with mood-congruent psychotic features. High acute risk.
Recommendation: inpatient psychiatric admission (she agrees to voluntary). 1:1 observation in ED. Restart sertraline; add an antipsychotic on the unit.

INPATIENT PSYCHIATRIC UNIT, REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/26/2026 (voluntary) — discharged 06/12/2026.

Diagnosis: major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe, with psychotic features (mood-congruent guilt delusion). Medical: generalized epilepsy, central DI, HIV (suppressed), treated cerebral toxoplasmosis.

Course: Sertraline restarted at 50 mg and increased to 100 mg daily on day 5. Olanzapine started 5 mg at bedtime, increased to 10 mg on day 4. Over the second week sleep and appetite improved, she began eating full meals, and the belief that her illnesses were deserved punishment loosened and then faded. Suicidal ideation resolved by day 12; she engaged in safety planning and groups. No seizures; phenytoin, desmopressin and Biktarvy continued. Sodium normal on repeat. Roommate confirmed the collected pills were disposed of and her own medications are locked.

At discharge: denies SI/HI, no psychotic symptoms, future-oriented (her daughter, a work project).

Discharge medications: sertraline 100 mg daily; olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime; phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS; desmopressin 0.1 mg BID; Biktarvy daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis); latex.

TCM visit after inpatient psychiatry 5/26–6/12.

ED 5/25: roommate found a suicide note; detailed overdose plan with collected pills; had stopped sertraline about three months earlier. Diagnosed severe recurrent MDD with psychotic features (guilt delusion). Restarted sertraline 100, olanzapine 10 qHS. Discharge summary reviewed. In hindsight, the December cancellation and March no-show fall in the stretch when she was getting worse.

Today: came with roommate. "Better than I was, not good yet." Sleeping 8–9 h. Eating more. Belief that she deserves her illnesses "isn't there the way it was." PHQ-9 17. Denies suicidal ideation, intent or plan since the second week of admission; no preparatory behavior. Protective: daughter, roommate. Means: roommate holds all meds in a lockbox, pills from May were disposed of. Reviewed safety plan together; she can name her steps and contacts.

Meds: sertraline 100, olanzapine 10 qHS, phenytoin ER 300 qHS, desmopressin 0.1 BID, Biktarvy, folic acid, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 53.5 kg (61.5 kg a year ago). Thin. Poor-to-fair eye contact, soft speech, affect depressed but reactive at times; no evidence of psychosis. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
1. MDD, recurrent, severe with psychotic features — early recovery, still moderate-severe symptoms. Continue sertraline 100 and olanzapine 10. Risk reviewed and documented; acute risk not imminent given engagement, safety plan, means restriction and supports; follow closely. Weekly therapy starts 6/19. Psychiatry 8/11. I'll call her in 2 weeks; visit in 5 weeks. 988/crisis numbers re-given.
